sources.title: Lectures on Nonparametric Bayesian Statistics
sources.locator: §8.1, equation (8.2); §7.3, Theorem 7.5 and proof, printed pp. 39–40; §7.8, Theorem 7.8 denominator/test proof, printed pp. 41–42; §9.4, Lemma 9.8.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete relevant full-text sections in the 134-page UvA PDF. Equation (8.2) fixes the root-L2 convention. Theorem 7.5 assumes a KL property and tests with errors tending to zero; its proof amplifies one sufficiently accurate test over independent blocks using Hoeffding. Theorem 7.8 gives the KL-neighborhood denominator bound and the tested-numerator route. Lemma 9.8 gives the L1/Hellinger comparisons. Local items supply full proofs under this library’s explicit measure-theoretic conventions.

contents.name: Root-L2 Hellinger definition
contents.support: The source defines the same root-L2 normalization; the item additionally states supplied finite-valued densities, the common sigma-finite dominator, and finiteness.

contents.name: Hellinger comparison with density L1
contents.support: The source states the root-L2 inequalities between Hellinger and density L1. The local proof supplies the canonical P+Q invariance argument and derives the event-supremum TV factor.

contents.name: Schwartz posterior consistency and block test amplification
contents.support: The source proves strong consistency from KL support and uniformly consistent tests, and explicitly amplifies a fixed test by independent blocks. The local theorem proves its denominator, numerator, measurable-kernel and finite-positive-fibre details.

contents.name: Integrated-likelihood denominator and test-splitting proof
contents.support: The source gives the integrated likelihood lower-bound and tested numerator structure. The local proof supplies the full argument under the stated joint-density, IID, summability, and library AC hypotheses.

sources.title: The Bernstein-Von-Mises Theorem under Misspecification
sources.locator: §4.1, Lemma 4.1 and its complete proof, printed pp. 376–378; Corollaries 4.1–4.2, printed pp. 378–379.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete published 29-page PDF and all of §4.1. Lemma 4.1 proves posterior exclusion by an exponential test split and a KL denominator; Corollary 4.1 obtains the almost-sure conclusion from test errors tending to zero after test amplification; Corollary 4.2 states the metric-separated consistency variant. The local result is the well-specified dominated IID specialization with summable input errors and a complete direct proof.

contents.name: Posterior exclusion by KL mass and uniform tests
contents.support: In the well-specified special case the likelihood-tilted measures in the source reduce to the model product laws. The local proof establishes its own denominator lower bound, block amplification, numerator bound, and Borel–Cantelli conclusion.

contents.name: Consistency from tests whose errors tend to zero
contents.support: The corollary confirms the almost-sure testing route. The local theorem states summable errors and derives the exponential block-test bound rather than importing a proof.

contents.name: Metric-separated posterior consistency
contents.support: The corollary supplies the metric-separated scope. The local item adds the exact dominated-kernel and joint-density hypotheses needed by this library.

alternatives.argument: The supplied-density definition is fully local: square-root measurability follows from threshold preimages, and the bound (sqrt(p)-sqrt(q))^2 <= p+q proves finiteness by additivity. The accessible full lecture notes give the same normalization.

The complete local proof constructs P+Q, derives both supplied densities against it, proves invariance, derives event-supremum TV as half the density L1 distance, and applies Holder pointwise. The accessible full lecture notes state the density L1/Hellinger inequalities.

The complete local proof proves a KL denominator lower bound by log-ratio integrability, Jensen and the IID strong law; amplifies summable tests by independent blocks and Hoeffding; integrates the tested numerator with Tonelli; and applies Markov and Borel–Cantelli. The accessible Kleijn notes and KvdV paper give independent full-text treatments of the consistency route.
